To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
progesterone induces a specific, rapid and transient increase in the synthesis of a 17 kDa protein in human endometrial stromal cells.

the human endometrial cell contains a specific, high affinity, cytosolic receptor for progesterone that can be demonstrated in vitro by a variety of techniques, and that this receptor is capable of binding and translocating to the nucleus and of inducing specific protein synthesis in vitro.
the progesterone receptor (PR) in human endometrial stromal cells is the same as the PR in human breast cancer cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the steroid receptor proteins and their biological activities in human endometrial tissue.
the identification of progesterone-dependent secretory proteins from the endometrium of the human uterus and their role in endometrial differentiation.

the isolation and characterization of progesterone receptors and the identification of specific proteins secreted by progesterone-treated human endometrium that are under the control of these receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding of a steroid to a tissue-specific receptor in a target cell is the initial event in the mechanism of steroid action.
the receptor is the “molecular” mediator of steroid hormone action.
the receptor is the mediator of the hormone’s action.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified several proteins that bind progesterone with high affinity and that are secreted by human decidua in response to progesterone.
we have identified and characterized the progesterone receptor (PR) of human endometrium and have demonstrated its correlation with progesterone-dependent biological activity.
progesterone is an important regulator of human endometrial function, but that the mechanism of action is still unknown.
The main takeaway from our work is that
progesterone and estrogen are both important for maintaining the pregnancy and that progesterone is more important for the first trimester and estrogen more important in the third trimester.
progesterone is a potent modulator of the endometrial secretome.
we have shown that progesterone can act as a transcriptional activator in endometrial cells and that this action can be inhibited by RU486.
